Vijeta Patel W/o Shri Laxmi Narayan Patel Aged About 38 Years R/o Village Kumhari, Tehsil Tundra, District : Balodabazar-Bhathapara, Chhattisgarh. ---- Petitioner Versus 1. State Of Chhattisgarh Through The Secretary, Department Of Panchayat And Rural Development, Atal Nagar, Naya Raipur, District : Raipur, Chhattisgarh. 2. The Commissioner, Division Raipur, District : Raipur, Chhattisgarh. 3. The Collector, District Baloda Bazar Bhatapara Chhattisgarh. 4. The Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue)/Prescribed Authority Giraudh, District Baloda Bazar Bhatapara Chhattisgarh. 5. Gram Panchayat Kumhari, Through The Secretary, Village Kumhari, Janpad Panchayat Tundra, District Baloda Bazar Bhatapara Chhattisgarh. 6. Rajesh Sahu S/o Dhaniram Sahu R/o Village Kumhari, Block Kasdol, District Baloda Bazar Bhatapara Chhattisgarh. 7. Sadhram Patel S/o Pulang Patel R/o Village Kumhari Block Kasdol, District Baloda Bazar Bhatapara Chhattisgarh. ---- Respondents (Cause Title taken from Case Information System) For Petitioner : Mr. Prateek Sharma, Advocate For Res./State : Mr. Soumitra Kesharwani, Panel Lawyer For Respondent No. 7 : Mr. Sunil Sahu, Advocate Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rakesh Mohan Pandey Order on Board 04.04.2024 1.
texts.facts: By way of this petition, the petitioner has challenged the order dated 06.03.2024 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue), Giroud, District Baloudabazar, Bhatapara, whereby the petitioner, who was officiating Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat Kumhari, Tahshil- Tundra, District- Baloda Bazar, Bhatapara has been placed under suspension Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 according to the provisions of Section 39 (1)(b) of Chhattisgarh Panchayat Raj Adhiniyam, 1993 (henceforth "Adhiniyam, 1993"). 2. The facts of the present case are that the petitioner was elected as Surpanch of Gram Panchayat Kumhari in the year 2020. On 14.09.2021, Devnath and two other persons namely, Rajesh Sahu and Shankar Patel, who are residents of the same Gram Panchayat, moved an application under Section 40 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 making certain allegations with regard to financial irregularities before the Sub- Divisional Officer (Revenue)/ Prescribed Officer, Kasdol, District Baloda Bazar-Bhatapara. Smt. Vijeta Patel vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195381842/ 1 The concerned SDO (R), who is the prescribed authority, initiated the proceeding. An enquiry was conducted and its report was submitted on 23.11.2021. According to said report, allegations made against the petitioner were found false and fabricated. Thereafter, the complainants filed an appeal before the Collector, Balodabazar - Bhatapara against the order dated 30.11.2021 passed by the concerned SDO (R), whereby the proceedings pending against the petitioner were dropped. The Collector, vide its order dated 19.12.2022 remitted back the matter to the Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue), Kasdol to decide it afresh after affording a due opportunity of hearing to the complainants. The SDO (R), pursuant to the order passed by the Collector, again initiated proceedings under Section 40 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 against the petitioner and while exercising its power under Section 39(1)(b) of Adhiniyam, 1993 placed the petitioner under suspension vide order dated 06.03.2024, which is under challenge.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the complainants have no right to challenge the order passed by the Sub-Divisional Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 Officer (Revenue) in favour of the petitioner. He would further submit that in the enquiry initiated against the petitioner, she was exonerated and the proceedings pending before the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) were dropped therefore, no order of suspension would have been passed by the SDO (R) against the petitioner. 4. In support thereof, he placed reliance on the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Ravi Yashwant Bhoi Vs. Collector reported in 2012 (4) SCC 407 and would submit that the complainant cannot be a party to the lis and under the garb of being a necessary party, a person cannot be permitted to make a case as that of general public interest. The relevant paragraphs 58, 59 and 60 are reproduced herein below:- 58. Shri Chintaman Raghunath Gharat, Ex-President was the complainant, thus, at the most, he could lead the evidence as a witness. He could not claim the status of an adversial litigant. The complainant cannot be the party to the lis. A legal right is an averment of entitlement arising out of law. In fact, it is a benefit conferred upon a person by the rule of law. Thus, a person who uffers from legal injury can only challenge the act or omission. There may be some harm or loss that may not be wrongful in the eyes of law because it may not result in injury to a legal right or legally protected interest of the complainant but juridically harm of this description is called damnum sine injuria. 59. The complainant has to establish that he has been deprived of or denied of a legal right and he has sustained injury to any legally protected interest. 60. Under the garb of being necessary party, a person cannot be permitted to make a case as that of general public interest. A person having a remote interest cannot be Smt. Vijeta Patel vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195381842/ 2 permitted to become a party in the lis, as the person Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 wants to become a party in a case, has to establish that he has a proprietary right which has been or is threatened to be violated, for the reason that a legal injury creates a remedial right in the injured person. A person cannot be heard as a party unless he answers the description of aggrieved party............" 5. On the other hand, learned counsels appearing for the respondents would submit that the Sub-Divisional Officer (Revenue) has initiated a proceeding under Section 40 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 in pursuance of the order passed by the Collector, Baloda Bazar - Bhatapara dated 19.12.2022 and the petitioner has not challenged the very order in this petition. They would further submit that the order dated 19.12.2022 has already been challenged by the petitioner before the Commissioner by way of filing a revision which is still pending. They would also submit that the matter of the petitioner with regard to her suspension has been referred to the State Government according to the provisions of Section 39(2) of the Adhiniyam, 1993. They would further contend that an enquiry is pending against the petitioner before the Sub-Divisional Officer and while exercising power under Section 39(1)(b) of the Adhiniyam, 1993, the SDO (R), who is the prescribed authority, may place the office bearer under suspension, therefore the concerned SDO (R) is justified in passing the order impugned and the instant petition deserves to be dismissed. 7. Section 39 of the Adhiniyam, 1993 reads as under:- 39. Suspension of office-bearer of Panchayat. - (1) The prescribed authority may suspend from office any-office bearer,- Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 (a) against whom charges have been framed in any criminal proceedings under Chapter V A, Vi, IX, IX- A, X, XII, Sections 302, 303, 304-B, 305, 306, 312 to 318, 366-A, 366-B, 373 to 377 of Chapter XVI, Sections 395 to 398, 408, 409, 458 to 460 of Chapter XVII and Chapter XVIII of the Indian Penal Code, I860 (XLV of 1860) or under any Law for the time being in force for the prevention of adulteration of food stuff and drugs, suppression of immoral traffic in women and children, Protection of Civil Rights and Prevention of Corruption; or [(b) on whom, show cause notice along with charge-sheet under this Act, has been served for removal from office.] (2) The order of suspension under sub-section (1) shall be reported to the State Government within a period of ten days and shall be subject to such orders as the State Government may deem fit to pass. If the order of suspension is not confirmed by the State Government within 90 days from the dale of receipt of such report it shall be deemed lo have vacated. (3) In the event that the Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat, President of Janpad Panchayat or Zila Panchayat, as the case may be, is suspended under sub-section (1), the Secretary or the Chief Executive Officer of the concerned Panchayat shall cause to be called a special meeting of the Smt. Vijeta Patel vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195381842/ 3 Panchayat immediately, but not later than fifteen days from the date of receipt of information from prescribed authority and the members shall elect from amongst themselves, a person to hold the office of Sarpanch or President temporarily, as the case may be, and such officiating Sarpanch or President shall perform all the duties and exercise all the powers of Sarpanch or President, as the case may be, during the period for which such suspension continues : Provided that if the office of the Sarpanch or President is reserved for the member of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes or Other Backward Classes err for a woman, the officiating Sarpanch or President shall be elected from amongst the members belonging to the same category : Provided further that where the office of Sarpanch or President is reserved for a woman belonging to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes or Other Backward Classes and there is no other woman member of the Panchayat belonging, to that category who can be elected to officiate as Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12003 Sarpanch or President, as the case may be, any other woman member belonging to the other reserved categories, may be elected to officiate as Sarpanch or President as the case may be. (4) A person who has been suspended under sub-section (1) shall also forthwith stand suspended from the office of member or office-bearer of any other Panchayat of which he is a member or office-bearer. Smt. Vijeta Patel vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195381842/ 4 12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Ravi Yashwant Bhoi (supra) observed and held that the complainants cannot claim the status of an adversarial litigant and cannot be a party to the lis. It is further held that under the garb of being a necessary party, a person cannot be permitted to make a case as that of general public interest.
